exact_current_f2_sources.observation: ArtifactBoundPreHandoffReceipt is deterministically derived only after verify_release_archive accepts exact unopened ZIP bytes; it binds artifact SHA-256/size/name, manifest digest, source/build identities, archive policy digest and receipt ref.
Every successor clean-machine observation must match the exact artifact filename/SHA-256/size and artifact-subject digest before the historical generation-1 matrix is accepted.
Generation 3 requires the external receipt bytes to equal ArtifactBoundPreHandoffReceipt.canonical_bytes() exactly, then binds receipt SHA-256/size/ref into successor observations.
The canonical archive policy uses ZIP_STORED and explicit canonical metadata; the verifier rebuilds canonical archive bytes and requires exact whole-archive byte equality.
Generation 3 is accepted only at repository-hosted CI scope; no final release ZIP, external receipt, real clean-machine execution or runtime/whole-system credit is observed.

primary_external_sources.observation: SLSA provenance verification separately verifies the provenance envelope signature/root of trust and checks that the statement subject digest matches the artifact.
Blob verification can bind an artifact digest to a signer identity/certificate/root, including bundle-based offline verification data.
Keyless signing introduces OIDC identity, short-lived certificates and transparency-log witnessing; these are additional trust infrastructure, not mere content hashing.
DSSE authenticates a payload plus payload type with one or more signatures; keyid is only an unauthenticated hint.

source_level_distinction.content_identity: F2 already provides strong exact-byte content identity for artifact and external receipt.
source_level_distinction.origin_identity: No cryptographic signer/origin authentication mechanism was found in the inspected F2 handoff path.
source_level_distinction.security_meaning: These are distinct properties. Missing signature does not imply missing content integrity; adding a signature does not replace local artifact/payload verification.

open_question_for_e2: Does F2 currently rely on any non-recomputable producer assertion or untrusted distribution boundary such that signer-origin authentication changes the next clean-machine acceptance predicate, or can the receiver recompute all authoritative receipt semantics from the exact artifact plus fixed policy?
